logline: 믿는 수녀와 의심하는 과학 유튜버, 8년 전 절교한 두 친구가 사라진 사람의 흔적을 쫓아 하노이에서 메콩강까지 국경을 넘는다
destination: 소설 태양 아래 올리브에서 만날 수 있습니다
setting: 기후 위기의 한국 시골과 수녀원, 서울의 작은 스튜디오, 하노이 근교의 강, 라오스 열차, 메콩강 강둑, 태국 북부 숲의 산길
anchor: a slender Korean nun in her late twenties with a bright open grown-up face and short black hair under a short pale blue veil, in a simple pale blue habit
palette: silver green, pale gold, sky blue, warm beige, deep teal
withheld: 이레가 잃어버린 기억과 몸의 비밀, 준의 정체, 길 끝에서 드러나는 진실

beats.beat: 폭염의 시골 길가, 있어서는 안 될 올리브
beats.visual: a blazing summer noon on a Korean countryside lane: at frame centre, at the edge of the cracked asphalt beside a green rice paddy, stands a lone young olive tree with a twisted pale grey trunk and narrow silver-green leaves that flash silver whenever the hot wind turns them, out of place among the rice plants; the sun is high and white, and heat shimmer wavers over the road and the fields; low farmhouses with grey tin roofs sit far back along the lane, and green hills close the view behind them under a hazy pale sky; a single dragonfly hovers above the paddy water; the asphalt is bleached and split by the heat, tufts of dry grass in the cracks; the scene is bright, still and strange, one tree from a far hotter country rooted where it should not be
beats.motion: the hot wind turns the leaves of the olive tree, and that turning of leaves is the one movement in the shot: at the start the narrow leaves hang still and green; over the whole five seconds a slow hot breeze moves through the tree from left to right, flipping the leaves so their silver undersides flash in the noon light and settle back green, again and again, the thin branches swaying gently with them; the twisted grey trunk stays rooted and still; the rice plants in the paddy lean very slightly in the same breeze; the cracked asphalt, the farmhouses, the hills and the hazy sky stay completely still; the heat shimmer over the road wavers steadily; every other thing in the frame holds perfectly still from the first moment to the last; the camera holds a medium wide shot of the tree from across the lane, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 그 올리브를 본 이레 — 재난 현장을 누비는 수녀
beats.visual: the same blazing countryside lane: the slender Korean nun in her late twenties with a bright open grown-up face and short black hair under a short pale blue veil stands at frame left in her simple pale blue cotton habit, muddy rubber boots on her feet and a heavy canvas tote of bottled water over one shoulder, facing the lone olive tree at frame right in three-quarter view; one hand shades her eyes as she looks up at the silver-green leaves, her lips parted in wonder, a small plain wooden cross on a cord at her chest; a light sheen of sweat shows on her brow; behind her the rice paddies shine and the green hills shimmer in the heat; dried mud is caked on the hem of her habit from a morning of relief work; the sky is white and hot; the moment is curious and tender, a nun stopped short by a tree that should not be here
beats.motion: the nun tilts her head slowly back to look up into the olive tree, and that lifting gaze is the one movement in the shot: at the start she stands shading her eyes, looking at the lower branches; over the whole five seconds her face lifts slowly toward the top of the tree, her eyes drifting upward along the twisted trunk to the flashing leaves, a slow smile of wonder spreading across her face, while the edge of her pale blue veil stirs in the hot breeze; her body, her boots and the heavy canvas tote stay planted where they are; the olive leaves flicker silver in the same breeze; the rice paddies, the farmhouses and the hills stay completely still; the heat shimmer wavers steadily; the camera holds a medium shot of the nun and the tree from the side of the lane, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 도움이 필요한 곳이면 몸이 먼저 나가는 이레
beats.visual: a Korean village street the morning after a summer flood: brown mud dries in a crust across the road, soaked wooden furniture and mattresses are stacked by the doorways, and grey sandbags line the walls; at frame centre the slender Korean nun in her late twenties in her pale blue cotton habit, sleeves pushed up and rubber boots caked with mud, kneels on a flattened cardboard sheet in front of an old village woman in a flowered work vest who sits on a low plastic stool; the nun holds both of the old woman's hands in hers, her bright face turned up to her with complete attention, listening; the old woman's weathered face is creased with worry; a plain white relief canopy stands behind them with stacks of bottled water under it; morning sun lights the wet mud so it glistens; the street smells of wet earth and hard work, and the nun is the calmest point in it
beats.motion: the nun gently presses the old woman's hands as she listens, and that pressing is the one movement in the shot: at the start she kneels holding both hands, looking up; over the whole five seconds her thumbs move slowly across the backs of the old woman's knuckles and she nods a little, her face softening into a reassuring smile, while the old woman's shoulders ease down slowly from their hunch; their joined hands stay in the centre of the frame; the stacked furniture, the sandbags, the relief canopy and the bottled water stay completely still; the drying mud on the road glistens unchanged in the morning sun; the soaked mattresses by the doorway and the grey sandbags hold their places in the bright morning; the camera holds a medium shot at the nun's kneeling height, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 그런 이레와 달리 맹신을 파고드는 과학 채널 미놋의 솔민
beats.visual: night in a small cluttered home studio: the lean sharp-eyed Korean woman with a short black bob and thin silver-rimmed glasses sits at frame centre at her desk in a loose charcoal linen shirt with rolled sleeves, facing the camera, speaking into a microphone on a boom arm; she holds up between two fingers a small clear glass bottle of cloudy water, studying it with one eyebrow raised and a dry, unimpressed half smile; on the desk in front of her lie a slim digital water-testing pen and a small notebook closed shut; a round ring light behind the camera throws a bright even glow on her face; shelves of books with plain worn spines and a wiped-blank whiteboard fill the wall behind her; a coffee mug has left rings on the desk; the room is lit only by the ring light and a small desk lamp, the night outside the window black; she is sharp, amused and impossible to fool
beats.motion: the woman slowly turns the little glass bottle in front of the ring light, and that turning bottle is the one movement in the shot: at the start she holds the bottle still between two fingers, eyebrow raised; over the whole five seconds she rotates it slowly in the bright light so the cloudy water swirls and glints inside the glass, her eyes narrowing behind her silver-rimmed glasses and her dry half smile widening at one corner; her elbow stays planted on the desk; the microphone on its boom arm, the water-testing pen, the closed notebook and the coffee mug stay completely still; the bookshelves and the blank whiteboard behind her hold unchanged; the ring light glow stays steady; every other thing in the frame holds perfectly still from the first moment to the last; the camera holds a medium close shot across the desk at her eye level, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 이레에게 믿음은 숨, 솔민에게 신앙은 검증할 대상
beats.visual: morning in a small plain convent chapel: tall clear windows pour broad bands of sunlight across rows of simple wooden pews and the whitewashed walls; at frame centre, standing alone in the front pew, the slender Korean nun in her late twenties in her pale blue habit and short pale blue veil sings with her eyes closed and her face lifted, her hands loosely clasped at her chest, her bright face completely open and at peace; a plain wooden cross hangs above the bare altar behind her; dust motes drift slowly through the sunlight; a small hymn book lies closed on the pew beside her; the air is warm and still; the stone floor gleams where the light touches it; the scene is quiet and luminous, faith as natural to her as breathing
beats.motion: the nun sings, and her slow breathing in the song is the one movement in the shot: at the start she stands with eyes closed and face lifted; over the whole five seconds her shoulders rise and sink gently with each long breath of the hymn, her lips moving softly, her face growing even more peaceful, while the dust motes drift slowly upward through the bands of sunlight around her; her clasped hands stay at her chest; the wooden pews, the closed hymn book, the bare altar and the wooden cross stay completely still; the bands of sunlight across the pews hold steady; the closed hymn book on the pew stays where it lies, and the plain wooden cross above the altar hangs motionless in the light; every other thing in the frame holds perfectly still from the first moment to the last; the camera holds a medium shot from the aisle at her chest height, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 가족 같던 이레와 솔민 — 아픈 말을 남기고 헤어진 지 8년
beats.visual: a small old rooftop flat in Seoul at dusk, with no one in it: through the single window the grey tiled rooftops of the old neighbourhood stretch away under a soft grey-gold evening sky; on the low wooden table in the middle of the narrow room stand two mismatched mugs, one pale blue and one charcoal grey, set far apart at opposite ends of the table, the pale blue one with a chip in its rim; two flat floor cushions lie on either side of the table, one pushed back crookedly against the wall; a rolled-up sleeping mat leans in the corner; a thin layer of dust lies on the windowsill and the table top; the last light lays a long warm stripe across the floor; the room is hushed and long unused, a small shared life left behind in silence
beats.motion: the last evening light slides slowly across the table toward the two mugs, and that sliding light is the one movement in the shot: at the start the warm stripe of light lies on the floor beside the table; over the whole five seconds it creeps slowly up over the table edge and across the dusty wooden top, reaching the chipped pale blue mug and lighting its rim while the charcoal mug at the far end stays in shade; the mugs, the cushions, the rolled mat and the window frame stay completely still; the tiled rooftops outside and the grey-gold sky hold unchanged; the thin dust on the windowsill stays as it is; the rolled sleeping mat in the corner leans unmoving, and the two flat cushions keep their crooked places on the floor; the camera holds a medium shot of the table from the doorway, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 어느 날 솔민에게 걸려 온 수상한 전화
beats.visual: late night in the small cluttered home studio: the lean sharp-eyed Korean woman with a short black bob and thin silver-rimmed glasses sits at her desk at frame centre in her loose charcoal linen shirt, a phone pressed to her ear, facing the camera; her free hand hangs frozen above the microphone switch, her brows drawn together in suspicion, her mouth slightly open on a question, her eyes fixed on the middle distance; the ring light is switched off now and only the small desk lamp lights one side of her face; the microphone on its boom arm, the camera on its tripod and the shelves of plain worn spines stand dim around her; the window behind is black; a cold cup of coffee sits by her elbow; the quiet room is suddenly tense, a call that should not have come
beats.motion: the woman listens hard to the voice on the phone, and her narrowing frown is the one movement in the shot: at the start she holds the phone to her ear with her brows drawn together; over the whole five seconds her frown deepens slowly, her eyes narrowing behind her silver-rimmed glasses and drifting slightly aside as she listens, her lips pressing together and parting again on an unspoken question, while her free hand stays frozen above the microphone switch; her shoulders and body stay facing the camera; the dark ring light, the microphone, the camera on its tripod and the cold coffee cup stay completely still; the desk lamp glow holds steady; the black window behind holds unchanged; every other thing in the frame holds perfectly still from the first moment to the last; the camera holds a medium close shot across the desk at her eye level, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 그 수녀회 마당, 8년 만에 마주한 솔민과 이레
beats.visual: a hot afternoon in the gravel courtyard of a small Korean convent: whitewashed walls and a low brick chapel with a plain wooden door frame the yard, potted plants line the wall, and a young olive tree stands in a large clay pot by the iron gate; at frame left, just inside the open gate, stands the lean sharp-eyed Korean woman with a short black bob and thin silver-rimmed glasses in her charcoal linen shirt, a backpack over one shoulder, stopped mid-step, her face caught between irritation and surprise; at frame right, beside the potted olive tree, stands the slender Korean nun in her late twenties in her pale blue habit and short veil, a green watering can in her hand, her bright face frozen with her mouth slightly open; the two face each other across the sunlit gravel; long afternoon shadows stretch from the wall; the moment is awkward, charged and full of eight years of silence
beats.motion: water trickles from the forgotten watering can in the nun's hand, and that trickle is the one movement in the shot: at the start the two women stand facing each other across the gravel; over the whole five seconds a thin stream of water keeps spilling slowly from the tilted spout onto the gravel at the nun's feet, darkening a small widening circle, while the two women stay frozen staring at each other, their faces unchanged; the woman's backpack stays on her shoulder; the potted olive tree, the iron gate, the chapel door and the potted plants stay completely still; the long afternoon shadows on the gravel hold steady; every other thing in the frame holds perfectly still from the first moment to the last; the camera holds a medium wide shot of the courtyard from the chapel steps, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 그 무렵 이레에게 닿은 소식 — 어린 날 세상을 가르쳐 준 준
beats.visual: night in a plain narrow convent bedroom: the slender Korean nun in her late twenties in her pale blue habit, her short veil laid aside on the bed so her short black hair shows, sits on the edge of the single iron bed at frame centre, holding open on her knees a small dented tin box of childhood keepsakes; inside the box lie a spiral seashell, a palm-sized globe with faded blue oceans, a smooth honey-coloured desert pebble and a folded sheet of paper showing small pencil dots joined by fine pencil lines; she looks down into the box with her round dark eyes soft and a small wistful smile on her lips; a small lamp on the bare wooden desk throws warm light across her and the box; a small wooden cross hangs on the whitewashed wall above the bed; the little window shows a plain dark night sky; the room is still, warm and full of an old, wide world
beats.motion: the nun's fingers move slowly over the keepsakes in the tin box, and that touching is the one movement in the shot: at the start her hands rest on the edges of the open box; over the whole five seconds her fingertips trail slowly across the spiral seashell, the little globe and the smooth desert pebble, turning the globe a quarter turn so its faded oceans glide past, while her eyes soften and a small warm smile forms on her lips; her body stays seated on the bed edge facing the camera; the folded pencil sheet, the laid-aside veil, the desk lamp and the wooden cross stay completely still; the warm lamp glow holds steady; every other thing in the frame holds perfectly still from the first moment to the last; the camera holds a medium close shot from the desk, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 사라진 준, 그리고 이레의 과거를 아는 듯한 낯선 이들
beats.visual: night outside the small Korean convent: the iron gate stands closed under a single dim lamp on the whitewashed wall, and the young olive tree in its clay pot is a dark shape just inside the bars; across the narrow street at frame right a long dark sedan is parked against the kerb with its engine running, its tinted windows solid black, its headlights dimmed to two faint pools on the asphalt and a thin plume of exhaust curling from its tail; the car is seen from the side and slightly behind so its plates do not show; the street is otherwise quiet, wet patches on the asphalt reflecting the lamp; a single moth circles the lamp above the gate; the convent windows are dark; the scene is still, watchful and wrong, the car idling outside the place where she sleeps
beats.motion: the single small moth circles slowly around the lamp above the gate, and that circling moth is the one movement in the shot: at the start the moth flutters just below the lamp; over the whole five seconds it loops in small slow circles through the warm lamplight, its pale wings catching the glow, never leaving the light above the gate; the dark sedan itself, its black windows, its dimmed headlights and its blank front, the closed iron gate, the potted olive tree and the dark convent windows stay completely still, and no smoke or steam rises from the car; the lamp glow on the wall holds steady; the wet patches on the asphalt hold their reflections; every other thing in the frame holds perfectly still from the first moment to the last; the camera holds a wide shot of the street from the convent side, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 준의 흔적을 쫓아 하노이로 국경을 넘는 이레와 솔민
beats.visual: inside a plane cabin descending toward Hanoi in bright tropical daylight: at the window seat at frame right sits the lean sharp-eyed Korean woman with a short black bob and thin silver-rimmed glasses, pressed back against her seat with arms folded and a pained, patient expression; leaning across her toward the window from the middle seat at frame left is the slender Korean nun in her late twenties in her pale blue habit and short veil, her bright face almost against the glass, eyes wide with delight; through the oval window the Red River delta spreads below, a wide brown river curling through bright green rice fields and tiny villages under a hazy sky; sunlight through the window lights both faces; the seat backs in front of them are plain grey; the moment is funny and warm, one delighted and one long-suffering
beats.motion: the nun leans further toward the window in delight, and that leaning is the one movement in the shot: at the start she leans across with her face near the glass; over the whole five seconds she presses slowly closer to the window, her eyes widening and a delighted grin spreading, while the woman at the window seat sinks a little deeper into her seat, her eyes drifting up toward the cabin ceiling in exasperation, her folded arms tightening; both stay seated in their places; the river and the rice fields far below slide very slowly across the oval window; the plain grey seat backs stay completely still; the bright tropical sunlight through the window holds steady; every other thing in the frame holds perfectly still from the first moment to the last; the camera holds a medium shot from the aisle at seated eye level, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 라오스행 열차에서도 사사건건 부딪치는 이레와 솔민
beats.visual: inside a modern Lao railway carriage in the afternoon: rows of clean blue seats face each other beside wide windows, and outside green jungle and misty limestone mountains slide past under a bright sky; at frame left, on one seat, the slender Korean nun in her late twenties in her pale blue habit and short veil leans forward talking animatedly, one hand raised mid-gesture, her bright face earnest; facing her at frame right, on the opposite seat, the lean sharp-eyed Korean woman with a short black bob and thin silver-rimmed glasses sits with arms crossed and one leg over the other, her eyes on the window and her mouth set in a flat, stubborn line; a small folding table between them holds two plastic water bottles and a paper bag of sticky rice; sunlight flickers across them through the passing trees; the carriage around them is calm; they are clearly in the middle of an argument neither will lose
beats.motion: the green jungle and misty mountains slide steadily past the train window, and that passing landscape is the one movement in the shot: at the start the window shows dense green trees; over the whole five seconds the jungle and the distant limestone mountains glide past from right to left in a smooth steady stream, their shadows flickering lightly across the two women, while the nun's raised hand stays mid-gesture and the woman opposite keeps her arms crossed, her eyes on the window; both stay seated facing each other; the blue seats, the folding table, the two water bottles and the paper bag stay completely still; the carriage interior holds steady; every other thing in the frame holds perfectly still from the first moment to the last; the camera holds a medium shot along the aisle at seated eye level, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 미행을 눈치채자 이레의 손목을 잡고 달리는 솔민
beats.visual: dusk on the bank of the wide brown Mekong river: a dirt path runs along the bank toward the camera between palm trees and wooden stilt houses, and long narrow wooden boats lie pulled up on the mud; low green mountains darken on the far shore under an amber and violet sky; running down the path toward the camera at frame centre, the lean sharp-eyed Korean woman with a short black bob and thin silver-rimmed glasses, in her charcoal linen shirt with no veil and no cross, grips the wrist of the slender Korean nun in her late twenties and pulls her along, her face fierce and focused, her crossbody bag bouncing; just behind her the nun runs in her pale blue habit, her short veil streaming back, her bright face startled but trusting; dust lifts from the path at their feet; lights are coming on in the stilt houses; the river glints behind them; the moment is breathless, two people suddenly running together
beats.motion: the two women run toward the camera along the riverbank path, and their running is the one movement in the shot: at the start they are a little way down the path, the woman pulling the nun by the wrist; over the whole five seconds they run steadily closer, staying at the centre of the frame, their strides quick, the nun's veil streaming back and the woman's bag bouncing, small puffs of dust lifting at each step, the woman's grip never letting go; their faces stay toward the camera; the boats on the mud, the palm trees, the stilt houses and the far mountains stay completely still; the brown river behind them glints slowly; the amber and violet dusk holds steady; every other thing in the frame holds perfectly still from the first moment to the last; the camera holds a medium wide shot down the path, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.beat: 믿는 이레와 의심하는 솔민 사이에도 진실한 우정이 있을까
beats.visual: dawn on a winding ochre dirt road through the misty green forest mountains of northern Thailand: tall teak trees and broad banana palms line the verge, and white mist lies in the valleys below the road; at frame centre, sitting side by side on a low mossy stone kerb at the roadside under a big teak tree, are the slender Korean nun in her late twenties in her dusty pale blue habit and short veil and the lean sharp-eyed Korean woman with a short black bob and thin silver-rimmed glasses in her charcoal linen shirt, with no veil and no cross; the woman is handing the nun a plastic water bottle without looking at her, eyes on the misty forest, a reluctant half smile at one corner of her mouth; the nun takes it, looking sideways at her with a tired, warm grin; both are dusty and tired; the first pale gold light spreads through the mist; the moment is quiet, a truce on a long road
beats.motion: the first pale gold dawn light spreads slowly through the mist onto the two women, and that spreading light is the one movement in the shot: at the start the road and the kerb lie in cool grey mist; over the whole five seconds warm pale light moves slowly down through the teak leaves and across the ochre road until it reaches the two women on the kerb, warming their tired faces, while the mist in the valley below drifts very slowly; the nun's hand and the woman's hand stay together on the water bottle between them; both stay seated side by side facing the camera; the teak trees, the banana palms and the stone kerb stay completely still; every other thing in the frame holds perfectly still from the first moment to the last; the camera holds a medium shot from across the road, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom

beats.visual: a quiet closing still of the Korean countryside lane in the golden late afternoon: the lone young olive tree stands at frame centre by the edge of the cracked asphalt beside the green rice paddy, its twisted pale grey trunk glowing and its narrow silver-green leaves shining silver in the low sun; long soft shadows stretch across the lane; the rice plants glow green and gold around it; the low farmhouses with grey tin roofs and the green hills behind lie in a warm haze; a small bird perches on the lowest branch; the sky is a soft clear gold; the heat of the day has eased; the tree stands rooted and alive where it was never meant to grow, and it looks entirely at home
beats.motion: the low golden sunlight shimmers through the olive leaves as a faint breeze stirs them, and that shimmering is the one movement in the shot: at the start the tree stands still in the golden light; over the whole five seconds a soft breeze moves gently through the branches so the narrow leaves turn slowly and flicker silver and green, their small shadows trembling on the asphalt, while the bird on the lowest branch shifts its weight once and settles; the twisted trunk stays rooted and still; the rice paddy, the farmhouses and the green hills stay completely still; the soft gold sky holds unchanged; the small bird's perch on the low branch stays steady, and the long soft shadows across the lane hold their shape; the camera holds a medium wide shot of the tree from across the lane, camera fixed, no tracking, no zoom
